prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He, You and I (1)/ shall arrange everything (2)/ and shall not ask them for help. (3)/ No error (4)
options: and shall not ask them for help.
explanation: For ordinary statements pronouns follow the 2-3-1 person order, so 'He, You and I' should be 'You, he and I'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: John, I and Hari have finished our studies. (a)/ (b)/ (c)/ No error (d)
explanation: The first-person pronoun comes last in such a series, so 'John, I and Hari' should be 'John, Hari and I'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: You, he and she have done her best (a)/ in the interview and it is sure (b)/ that all of them will pass. (c)/ No error (d)
options: You, he and she have done her best
in the interview and it is sure
that all of them will pass.
explanation: The compound subject 'You, he and she' is plural and third-personal, so the possessive must be 'their', not 'her'; correct to 'You, he and she have done their best'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: You and I have done (a)/ my best in (b)/ the examination (c)/ no error (d)
explanation: With the compound subject 'You and I', the possessive must be 'our', not 'my'; correct to 'have done our best in'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I and my colleague have carefully considered (a) / the important issues raised by the report (b) which you sent me / and we have decided to take the following action. (c) / no error (d)
options: I and my colleague have carefully considered
the important issues raised by the report which you sent me
and we have decided to take the following action.
explanation: When 'I' is joined with another noun as subject, 'I' comes last: 'My colleague and I have carefully considered'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: You, Mary and (A) me have (B) completed our work. (C) No error (D)
explanation: A subject pronoun is needed, not the objective 'me'; correct to 'You, Mary and I have completed our work.'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My sister and myself (1) / are pleased to accept (2) / your invitation to dinner. (3) / no error (4)
explanation: The reflexive 'myself' cannot serve as subject without an antecedent; use 'My sister and I are pleased to accept'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Madhuri and I have done my (1) / work patiently and diligently (2) / just for our safe and secure future. (3) / No Error (4)
options: Madhuri and I have done my
just for our safe and secure future.
explanation: The plural compound subject 'Madhuri and I' requires the possessive 'our', not 'my'; correct to 'Madhuri and I have done our'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Me and my friend have started working on a summer project which was approved by our teacher.
options: have started working on a summer project
explanation: 'Me' is objective and cannot be the subject, and 'I' should come last: 'My friend and I have started working'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I and my wife (1) / were declared (2) / the best couple at the party (3) / No error (4)
options: the best couple at the party
explanation: In a compound subject the first person 'I' is placed last: 'My wife and I were declared'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I and Tina will (1) / go to the market (2) / in the evening. (3) / No error (4)
explanation: Pronoun order requires 'I' at the end of a compound subject: 'Tina and I will go to the market'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: You, he and I (A) / must coordinate effectively to complete (B) / this project assignment by tomorrow evening. (C) / No Error (D)
options: this project assignment by tomorrow evening.
explanation: The pronoun order for a neutral/positive statement is correctly 2nd-3rd-1st person (You, he and I), and the plural verb 'must coordinate' agrees with the compound subject. No error.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I, you and he (A) / have committed a serious blunder (B) / during the accounting calculation process. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: Since the sentence confesses a blunder/fault, the correct pronoun order is 1st-2nd-3rd person ('I, you and he'), and the plural verb 'have committed' is right. No error.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My sister, Juliet, / got married / as her / was 23.
explanation: A clause subject needs the nominative pronoun and a time conjunction: 'when she was 23', not 'as her was 23'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I, you and she/ have been working happily/ in the same company and in the same branch/ for the last nine years.
options: in the same company and in the same branch
explanation: When pronouns of all three persons are joined in a positive statement, the order is 2-3-1: 'You, she and I'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Everybody stared / when me / entered the / drawing room.
explanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'entered', so the nominative form is needed: 'when I entered'.

sentence: In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg, / and me works on my short/ game with a baseball glove.
options: In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg
explanation: A compound subject needs the subject-case pronoun and a plural verb: 'Greg and I work on my short game', not 'and me works'.
